prompt: I would like to outperform the S&P 500 in the next year. Can you propose 10 stocks I should buy?
reply:
# 10 Stock Ideas for Trying to Beat the S&P 500

Most professional fund managers fail to beat the S&P 500 in a typical year, and over 10+ years roughly 85–90% fall behind (per S&P's SPIVA reports). So treat this as a list of ideas to research, not a reliable way to outperform. Also, my information runs through about May 2026, so prices and news from the last few months aren't reflected. Check current valuations before buying anything.

## The List

| # | Stock | Why it could beat the index | Main risk |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Taiwan Semiconductor (TSM)** | Makes nearly all the leading-edge chips for AI. It isn't in the S&P 500, so it makes your portfolio different from the index. | Tension between Taiwan and China; tariffs |
| 2 | **Broadcom (AVGO)** | Designs custom AI chips for Google, Meta and OpenAI, a fast-growing alternative to Nvidia. | High valuation; depends on a few large customers |
| 3 | **Micron (MU)** | Strong demand for the high-bandwidth memory used in AI chips, and memory prices have been tight. | Memory is a boom-and-bust business, and it may be near a peak |
| 4 | **Alphabet (GOOGL)** | Growth in Gemini, Google Cloud and its TPU chips (including a large deal with Anthropic), plus Waymo. | AI chatbots could eat into Search; antitrust cases |
| 5 | **Amazon (AWS)** | AWS growth is speeding up again, and its own Trainium chips could raise profit margins. | Heavy spending weighs on free cash flow |
| 6 | **Vertiv (VRT)** | Supplies power and cooling equipment for data centers. | Would fall hard if AI data-center spending slows |
| 7 | **GE Vernova (GEV)** | Has years of orders for gas turbines and grid equipment as electricity demand rises. | Valuation already assumes strong execution |
| 8 | **Constellation Energy (CEG)** | Largest U.S. nuclear operator, signing long-term power deals with tech companies (e.g., restarting Three Mile Island for Microsoft). | Regulation; power prices |
| 9 | **Eli Lilly (LLY)** | Leads in weight-loss drugs, with its oral pill orforglipron as a new growth driver. | Drug-price pressure; competition; high valuation |
| 10 | **JPMorgan Chase (JPM)** | The best-run large bank. Adds a non-tech holding, with support from lighter regulation and deal-making. | Recession; credit losses |

## About This List

- **It's a concentrated bet on AI.** About 8 of the 10 depend on AI and data-center spending continuing. That's the main reason it could beat the index, and also why it could lag badly if that spending slows. For more balance, you could swap Micron and Vertiv for steadier companies like Costco or Visa, or an energy company like ExxonMobil.
- **You have to be different from the index to beat it.** The S&P 500 is already about 35% big tech, so buying Nvidia, Microsoft and Apple mostly just copies it. That's why this list includes companies outside the index (TSM) and ones that are small parts of it.

## How to Approach It

- **Keep most of your money in an index fund.** A common setup is 70–80% in an S&P 500 fund and 20–30% in individual picks like these. You still get the chance to outperform, but a bad year won't wreck your portfolio.
- **Split the money evenly** (about 10% of your stock-picking money each) so no single company can sink the portfolio.
- **Write down why you bought each one.** Then sell based on whether that reason still holds, not on price swings.
- **Mind taxes.** In many countries, gains on stocks held under a year are taxed at a higher rate.

This isn't personalized financial advice. Your age, goals, risk tolerance and tax situation all matter. If you tell me more about those, I can adjust the list.
